items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or equivalent experience /training.
Supervisory & personnel management experience and leadership in assessment and prioritization of employee performance, workflow and collaboration/teamwork.
Five (5) years of related experience/training OR eight (8) years related experience education/training.
Extensive experience providing high level accounting, audit and payroll principles and procedures with revenue-generating and clearing accounts.

Experience and proven success in clinic/center management experience, with progressive expertise in practice management, scheduling, customer-service methods, incident reporting, regulatory compliance, accreditation requirements, and information technology.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Hobbs Veterinary Specialty Hospital Business Officer is responsible for financial, budget, human resource administration and facilities management of the San Diego clinic. In collaboration with the COO, this position oversees all unit financial and budget activities, including personnel and operating budgets and supervises the financial processing, administrative and clerical functions at this location. This position will work closely with senior leadership, managers, supervisors and staff in their assigned units to ensure business and administrative needs are met. The San Diego veterinary clinic is a fast-paced business center, constantly evolving with a demanding clientele and veterinary patient case load.

Combination of human resources, leadership, complex accounting, and organizational skills to oversee a complex, self-supporting unit in the areas of teaching, research, clinical service, information technology, space and facility management.

Knowledge of or ability to quickly learn University accounting, payroll, UC policies and procedures, and collective bargaining agreements/contracts and analytical skills to discern and apply appropriately.

Interpersonal, oral and written communication skills to interact with a diverse group of people to include UC administration, faculty, clinicians, clinical trainees, campus personnel, vendors and clients.
Ability to effectively carry out leadership and delegation of authority.
Skills to communicate with discretion and confidence with regard to confidential material or situations and exercise judgment in releasing information.
